liturgical.title_en: Saints Cornelius, Pope, and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs
liturgical.title_vi: Saints Cornelius, Pope, and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs

primary.title_en: Saints Cornelius, Pope, and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs
primary.title_vi: Saints Cornelius, Pope, and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs
primary.summary_en: This memorial honors Saint Cornelius, Pope, and Saint Cyprian, Bishop, martyrs celebrated together for their shared witness to faith and unity. Cornelius defended the Church's mercy during the Novatian schism, while Cyprian articulated the centrality of ecclesial unity. Their feast highlights the interplay between papal authority and episcopal communion.
primary.summary_vi: This memorial honors Saint Cornelius, Pope, and Saint Cyprian, Bishop, martyrs celebrated together for their shared witness to faith and unity. Cornelius defended the Church's mercy during the Novatian schism, while Cyprian articulated the centrality of ecclesial unity. Their feast highlights the interplay between papal authority and episcopal communion.
primary.body_en: Saint Cornelius, who served as Pope from 251 to 253 AD, faced the crisis of the Decian persecution and the subsequent Novatian schism regarding the readmission of lapsed Christians. He steadfastly taught that the Church possesses the power to forgive sins and admit penitents back into communion, standing in firm opposition to the rigorism of Novatian. His contemporary, Saint Cyprian of Carthage, supported Cornelius's stance and developed influential teachings on the nature of the Church, most notably his famous assertion that 'the Church is a single body, and it is not possible that she should be divided.' Their friendship and mutual support provide a foundational model for the relationship between the Roman See and the local churches, emphasizing that unity in faith requires both hierarchical order and collegial respect. Together, they exemplify the pastoral courage needed to preserve doctrinal truth and charitable mercy during times of intense persecution and internal division.

liturgical.title_en: Thursday of the 24th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Năm tuần 24 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Thursday of the 24th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Năm tuần 24 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Thursday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Thursday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Thursday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Thursday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

primary.summary_en: The Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time is a day of reflection on divine generosity and the mystery of God's grace, as articulated in the Gospel of the laborers in the vineyard. The liturgical color is green, symbolizing hope and life in the Holy Spirit, guiding the faithful through the ordinary time of the year. This Sunday invites believers to contemplate the unexpected nature of God's justice and the universal call to holiness.

primary.body_en: On this Sunday, the Church proclaims the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard (Mt 20:1-16a), challenging the faithful to reconsider their understanding of merit and reward. The readings emphasize that God's ways are not like human ways, as highlighted in the First Reading from Isaiah 55:6-9, which calls for a conversion of heart and mind. St. Paul’s letter to the Philippians (1:20c-24, 27a) further encourages the community to stand firm in one spirit, striving together for the faith of the gospel. This day serves as a reminder that salvation is a gift of grace, not a wage earned by human effort alone, urging believers to trust in God's boundless mercy rather than their own righteousness.

liturgical.title_en: Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist
liturgical.title_vi: Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist

primary.title_en: Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist
primary.title_vi: Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist
primary.summary_en: Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist is commemorated on September 21, marking a significant Feast in the Catholic liturgical calendar. The liturgical texts for this day emphasize the unity of the Church and the call to conversion, centering on the Gospel of Matthew. As one of the twelve Apostles, Matthew is traditionally credited with authoring the first Gospel of the New Testament, originally in Aramaic before its Greek transmission.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist is commemorated on September 21, marking a significant Feast in the Catholic liturgical calendar. The liturgical texts for this day emphasize the unity of the Church and the call to conversion, centering on the Gospel of Matthew. As one of the twelve Apostles, Matthew is traditionally credited with authoring the first Gospel of the New Testament, originally in Aramaic before its Greek transmission.
primary.body_en: The Feast of Saint Matthew highlights his pivotal role as both an Apostle and Evangelist, bridging the Jewish heritage and the Christian faith. Liturgical readings draw from Ephesians 4:1-7, 11-13 and Matthew 9:9-13, illustrating the diversity of gifts within the Church and the call of Levi to follow Christ. This day reminds the faithful of the importance of understanding Scripture and embracing the call to discipleship, as Matthew’s Gospel provides essential teachings on the Kingdom of Heaven. His life serves as a model of transformation, moving from a tax collector in Capernaum to a witness of the Divine Word, ensuring that the Church remains rooted in apostolic teaching and prophetic tradition.

liturgical.title_en: Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, Priest
liturgical.title_vi: Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, Priest

primary.title_en: Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, Priest
primary.title_vi: Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, Priest
primary.summary_en: The Church celebrates the memorial of Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, a Capuchin friar known for the stigmata and profound prayer life. This feast, fixed on September 23, invites the faithful to emulate his humility, obedience, and devotion to the Eucharist.
primary.summary_vi: The Church celebrates the memorial of Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, a Capuchin friar known for the stigmata and profound prayer life. This feast, fixed on September 23, invites the faithful to emulate his humility, obedience, and devotion to the Eucharist.
primary.body_en: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina (1887–1968) remains a central figure in modern Catholic spirituality, celebrated for his mystical gifts and unshakeable faith. On this memorial, the liturgy emphasizes the call to radical trust in Divine Providence, resonating with the First Reading from Proverbs and the Gospel of Luke, which narrate Christ's commissioning of the apostles. His life serves as a testament to the power of the Cross and the importance of humble service within the Church. Beloved for his stigmata and compassionate ministry, St. Pio reminds the faithful that true sanctity is found in daily obedience and love for neighbor. This memorial is observed universally in the Latin Church, with white vestments signifying the joy of his heavenly victory and priestly fidelity.

liturgical.title_en: Thursday of the 25th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Năm tuần 25 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Thursday of the 25th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Năm tuần 25 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Thursday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Thursday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Thursday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Thursday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

primary.summary_en: The Twenty-sixth Sunday in Ordinary Time is celebrated on September 27, 2026, in the Roman Catholic liturgical calendar. The liturgical readings focus on God's justice and mercy, inviting the faithful to repentance and obedience through the parables and prophetic texts appointed for this day.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Chủ Nhật này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en: On this Sunday, the liturgical narrative centers on the dynamic relationship between divine justice and human repentance, as highlighted in the first reading from Ezekiel (18:25-28), where the Lord assures that no past sin can condemn those who turn to righteousness. The Gospel reading from Matthew (21:28-32) further elucidates this theme through the Parable of the Two Sons, contrasting verbal obedience with actual deed, emphasizing that true righteousness is found in following God's will rather than merely speaking about it. This day, situated within the late stages of Ordinary Time, calls the faithful to examine the authenticity of their faith and respond to God's call with genuine conversion and humility, mirroring the kenotic hymn of Christ found in the second reading from Philippians.

liturgical.title_en: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels
liturgical.title_vi: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels

primary.title_en: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels
primary.title_vi: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels
primary.summary_en: The Feast of Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael honors the three archangels identified by name in Scripture. Michael is known for his defense of God and his people, Gabriel for his role as a messenger, and Raphael for his assistance to those in need. This celebration underscores the role of angels in divine providence and salvation history.
primary.summary_vi: The Feast of Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael honors the three archangels identified by name in Scripture. Michael is known for his defense of God and his people, Gabriel for his role as a messenger, and Raphael for his assistance to those in need. This celebration underscores the role of angels in divine providence and salvation history.
primary.body_en: On this Feast, the Church commemorates the three archangels who serve as principal messengers and defenders of divine will. Michael, meaning 'Who is like God?', stands as the prince of the heavenly host, depicted in Revelation leading the armies against the dragon. Gabriel, meaning 'God is my strength', brings crucial revelations, notably the Annunciation to the Virgin Mary, acting as a bridge between heaven and earth. Raphael, meaning 'God heals', appears in the Book of Tobit to guide and heal, demonstrating divine mercy and care. Together, they represent the full spectrum of angelic ministry: warfare against evil, transmission of truth, and healing service to humanity.

primary.title_en: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus, Virgin and Doctor of the Church
primary.title_vi: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus, Virgin and Doctor of the Church
primary.summary_en: The Church celebrates the Memorial of Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus, a Carmelite nun and Doctor of the Church. Known as 'The Little Flower,' she entered the convent at age 15 and died on September 30, 1897. Her spirituality of spiritual childhood emphasized simplicity, trust, and love in everyday life.
primary.summary_vi: The Church celebrates the Memorial of Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus, a Carmelite nun and Doctor of the Church. primary.body_en:
Saint Thérèse of Lisieux, also known as Thérèse of the Child Jesus, is celebrated for her profound 'little way' of spiritual childhood, which teaches that holiness is accessible to everyone through small acts of love and total trust in God. Born Marie-Françoise-Thérèse Martin in Alençon, France, she entered the Carmel of Lisieux at age 15 and spent her brief life in prayer, sacrifice, and missionary support. Despite dying of tuberculosis at only 24 years old, her writings, particularly 'Story of a Soul,' have influenced countless believers and theologians, leading to her proclamation as a Doctor of the Church in 1997.

The liturgical readings for this Memorial include Job 19:21-27 and Luke 10:1-12. In Job, the patriarch expresses unshakable faith in his Redeemer, mirroring Thérèse’s steadfast hope despite suffering. In Luke, Jesus sends his disciples out in poverty and trust, a mission Thérèse embraced spiritually from her convent cell. Her legacy continues to challenge the faithful to seek greatness in humility and to find God in the ordinary moments of daily life, proving that sanctity is not measured by the size of one's works but by the love with which they are done.

liturgical.title_en: Saturday of the 26th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Bảy tuần 26 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Saturday of the 26th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Bảy tuần 26 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Saturday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Saturday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Saturday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Saturday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

primary.summary_en: Celebrated on October 4, 2026, this Sunday falls in Ordinary Time and is marked by liturgical green vestments. The readings focus on stewardship, divine judgment, and the fruits of faith, specifically drawing from Isaiah's Song of the Vineyard and the Parable of the Tenants in Matthew.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Chủ Nhật này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en: The Twenty-seventh Sunday in Ordinary Time invites the faithful to reflect on the relationship between God and His people through the lens of agriculture and stewardship. In the First Reading, Isaiah 5:1-7 presents the Song of the Vineyard, where Israel is depicted as a vineyard planted and cultivated by the Lord, only to yield wild grapes due to infidelity. This Old Testament metaphor finds its direct fulfillment in the Gospel of Matthew 21:33-43, where Jesus tells the Parable of the Tenants. In this parable, the landowner represents God, the vineyard represents Israel or the Kingdom, and the tenants represent the religious leaders who reject the prophets and ultimately the Son. The Gospel concludes with the solemn warning that the Kingdom will be taken away from those who refuse to produce its fruits and given to a people who will bear them. The Epistle from Philippians 4:6-9 provides the practical spiritual response to this call, urging believers to anxiety-free prayer, gratitude, and the meditation on whatever is true, noble, and right. Together, these readings challenge the congregation to examine their spiritual harvest and ensure their lives produce the fruits of justice and peace.

liturgical.title_en: Our Lady of the Rosary
liturgical.title_vi: Our Lady of the Rosary

primary.title_en: Our Lady of the Rosary
primary.title_vi: Our Lady of the Rosary
primary.summary_en: The Memorial of Our Lady of the Rosary is celebrated annually on October 7, honoring the Blessed Virgin Mary under the specific title associated with the devotion to the Rosary. This day highlights the scriptural mysteries of Christ's life, which are meditated upon through the prayers of the Hail Mary and the Our Father. It serves as a reminder of the power of this devotion in seeking Mary's intercession for the Church and the world.
primary.summary_vi: The Memorial of Our Lady of the Rosary is celebrated annually on October 7, honoring the Blessed Virgin Mary under the specific title associated with the devotion to the Rosary. This day highlights the scriptural mysteries of Christ's life, which are meditated upon through the prayers of the Hail Mary and the Our Father. It serves as a reminder of the power of this devotion in seeking Mary's intercession for the Church and the world.
primary.body_en:
The feast commemorates the victory at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571, which Pope Pius V attributed to the recitation of the Rosary by the faithful, a devotion he had ordered to be prayed universally. While originally a celebration of the Holy Rosary, the title emphasizes Mary's unique role in the history of salvation and her intimacy with the mysteries of her Son. In the modern liturgical calendar, this memorial invites the faithful to pause and contemplate the Gospel events that form the core of the Rosary mysteries.

The liturgical readings for the day, Galatians 2:1-2, 7-14 and Luke 11:1-4, provide a theological context for the devotion, pairing Paul's mission to the Gentiles with Jesus' teaching on prayer. These texts underscore the importance of correct doctrine and persistent prayer, elements central to the practice of the Rosary. The memorial encourages the faithful to integrate the rhythm of prayer with the meditation of sacred mysteries, fostering a deeper relationship with God through Christ and the intercession of Mary.

liturgical.title_en: Thursday of the 27th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Năm tuần 27 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Thursday of the 27th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Năm tuần 27 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Thursday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Thursday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Thursday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Thursday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

primary.title_en: Twenty-eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Chúa Nhật tuần 28 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: The Twenty-eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time focuses on the invitation to the divine banquet and the necessity of wearing the garment of grace. The liturgy pairs the promise of Isaiah's feast on Mount Zion with Paul's trust in God's provision in Philippians.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Chủ Nhật này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en: In this Sunday's liturgy, the faithful are reminded that God's providence provides for all needs, echoing St. Paul's declaration that he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him. The Gospel narrative of the wedding feast serves as a profound allegory for the Church, emphasizing that mere presence is insufficient; one must be clothed in the proper garment of conversion and charity to remain. This day challenges believers to examine whether their spiritual attire reflects a genuine readiness for the Lord's table, distinguishing between nominal adherence and authentic communion.

primary.summary_en: Saint Teresa of Jesus, also known as Teresa of Avila, was a sixteenth-century Spanish Carmelite nun and mystic who is honored as a Doctor of the Church for her profound writings on prayer and the interior life. Her legacy is deeply tied to the reform of the Carmelite Order and the promotion of mental prayer through works like The Interior Castle and The Way of Perfection.

Her legacy is deeply tied to the reform of the Carmelite Order and the promotion of mental prayer through works like The Interior Castle and The Way of Perfection.
primary.body_en: Teresa de Cepeda y Ahumada was born in Avila, Spain, in 1515 and entered the Carmelite Convent of the Incarnation at a young age. Her spiritual journey, marked by periods of dryness and intense mystical experiences, led her to initiate the reform of the Carmelite Order, emphasizing a return to the original rule of poverty and contemplation. She wrote extensively to guide her sisters and others in the practice of mental prayer, offering a systematic map of the soul's journey to union with God that remains foundational in Catholic theology. Pope Paul VI declared her the first woman to be named a Doctor of the Church in 1970, acknowledging her enduring theological contribution.

primary.title_en: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, Bishop and Martyr
primary.title_vi: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, Bishop and Martyr
primary.summary_en: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, Bishop and Martyr, is commemorated on October 17 as a memorial of a pivotal figure in early Church history and apostolic tradition. Celebrated in red vestments, the liturgy highlights his martyrdom and his profound theological writings composed during his journey to Rome. The day's official readings, Ephesians 1:15-23 and Luke 12:8-12, resonate with his emphasis on unity and faith. This observance honors his witness as the third bishop of Antioch and a student of the Apostle John.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, Bishop and Martyr, is commemorated on October 17 as a memorial of a pivotal figure in early Church history and apostolic tradition. Celebrated in red vestments, the liturgy highlights his martyrdom and his profound theological writings composed during his journey to Rome. The day's official readings, Ephesians 1:15-23 and Luke 12:8-12, resonate with his emphasis on unity and faith. This observance honors his witness as the third bishop of Antioch and a student of the Apostle John.
primary.body_en:
Saint Ignatius, often called Theophorus, served as the bishop of Antioch in Syria during the late first and early second centuries. According to tradition, he was instructed by the Apostle John and later succeeded Evodius. During the reign of Emperor Trajan, Ignatius was arrested and transported to Rome to be martyred by wild beasts in the Colosseum. Along his journey, he wrote seven concise letters to various churches and individuals, including the Church of Ephesus. These writings are crucial sources for understanding early Christian ecclesiology, particularly the doctrine of the episcopacy and the rejection of Docetism. His letters serve as a bridge between the apostolic age and the developing patristic theology.

The liturgical readings for this day include Ephesians 1:15-23 and Luke 12:8-12, chosen for their thematic resonance with Ignatian theology. The Epistle reading from Ephesians, which Ignatius himself wrote to during his journey, emphasizes the supremacy of Christ over all creation and the Church as His body. This aligns with Ignatius's own teachings on the necessity of unity with the bishop. The Gospel from Luke, where Jesus speaks of acknowledging Him before men, mirrors the courage Ignatius displayed in facing martyrdom. His famous desire to be 'wheat of Christ, ground by the teeth of beasts' reflects the steadfastness called for in the Gospel. The memorial thus invites the faithful to contemplate the cost of discipleship and the centrality of Christ in the life of the Church.

primary.summary_en: Saints John de Brébeuf and Isaac Jogues, Priests, and Companions, Martyrs are celebrated today as the North American Martyrs. They were Jesuit missionaries who served among the Huron and Mohawk peoples in the 17th century. Their lives ended in martyrdom during conflicts involving Native American tribes.

They were Jesuit missionaries who served among the Huron and Mohawk peoples in the 17th century. Their lives ended in martyrdom during conflicts involving Native American tribes.
primary.body_en: The Memorial of Saints John de Brébeuf and Isaac Jogues, Priests, and Companions, Martyrs honors eight Jesuit missionaries who worked in New France. John de Brébeuf is known for his linguistic work and his Huron catechism. Isaac Jogues endured severe torture among the Mohawks before ministering to settlers. Together with René Goupil, Jean de Lalande, Antoine Daniel, Gabriel Lalemant, Charles Garnier, and Noël Chabanel, they form the group known as the North American Martyrs. The liturgical readings of Ephesians 2:1-10 and Luke 12:13-21 emphasize God's grace and the folly of hoarding, contrasting earthly wealth with eternal life.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.

liturgical.title_en: Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles
liturgical.title_vi: Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles

primary.title_en: Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles
primary.title_vi: Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles
primary.summary_en: The Feast of Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles, is celebrated on October 28. It honors two of the original twelve disciples of Jesus Christ, traditionally commemorated together due to early Christian traditions linking their martyrdoms.
primary.summary_vi: The Feast of Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles, is celebrated on October 28. It honors two of the original twelve disciples of Jesus Christ, traditionally commemorated together due to early Christian traditions linking their martyrdoms.
primary.body_en: Saint Simon, often called the Zealot or the Cananean, is distinguished from Simon Peter in the Gospel lists, though little biographical detail is recorded. Tradition suggests he preached in Egypt and Persia before being martyred. Saint Jude, also known as Thaddeus, is the author of the Epistle of Jude and is patron of hopeless cases. The liturgy for this Feast emphasizes the unity of the apostolic mission and the foundation of the Church upon the apostles and prophets, as described in the first reading from Ephesians 2:19-22, which declares the faithful as fellow citizens with the holy ones and members of the household of God.

liturgical.title_en: Solemnity of All Saints
liturgical.title_vi: Đại Lễ Các Thánh Nam Nữ

primary.title_en: Solemnity of All Saints
primary.title_vi: Đại Lễ Các Thánh Nam Nữ
primary.summary_en: The Solemnity of All Saints celebrates the vast, innumerable multitude of holy men and women who have attained the beatific vision in heaven, including both canonized saints and the hidden, unsung faithful. The solemnity directs our gaze toward our heavenly homeland and renews our universal call to holiness.
primary.summary_vi: Đại Lễ Các Thánh Nam Nữ tôn vinh đoàn người đông đảo vô kể những người nam người nữ thánh thiện đã đạt tới vinh quang chiêm ngưỡng nhan Chúa trên thiên quốc, gồm cả các vị thánh được tuyên thánh và vô số tín hữu âm thầm trung kiên. Đại lễ hướng cái nhìn của chúng ta về quê trời đích thực và khơi dậy ơn gọi nên thánh phổ quát của mỗi người.
primary.body_en:
The origins of All Saints Day trace back to the early centuries of the Church, when the faithful commemorated all Christian martyrs on a single day following Pentecost. In the eighth century, Pope Gregory III dedicated a chapel in Saint Peter's Basilica to all the saints, apostles, martyrs, and confessors, fixing the date on November 1. Pope Gregory IV subsequently extended the solemnity to the universal Church in 835.

This solemnity celebrates the Church Triumphant in union with the Church Militant on earth and the Church Penitent in Purgatory. The Book of Revelation describes this heavenly gathering as 'a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and tribes, and peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne' (Rev 7:9).

The feast reminds every Christian that sanctity is achievable in every walk of life through the grace of Christ. In the Beatitudes proclaimed in today's Gospel, Jesus provides the divine charter for holiness.
primary.body_vi:
Nguồn gốc của Lễ Các Thánh bắt nguồn từ những thế kỷ đầu tiên của Giáo hội, khi các tín hữu mừng kính toàn thể các thánh tử đạo trong một ngày duy nhất sau Lễ Hiện Xuống. Vào thế kỷ thứ tám, Đức Giáo hoàng Grêgôriô III đã thánh hiến một nhà nguyện trong Vương cung Thánh đường Thánh Phêrô dâng kính toàn thể các thánh, tông đồ, tử đạo và hiển tu, ấn định ngày 1 tháng 11. Sau đó, Đức Giáo hoàng Grêgôriô IV đã mở rộng đại lễ này cho toàn thể Giáo hội vào năm 835.

Đại lễ này cử hành mầu nhiệm Giáo hội Chiến Thắng trong sự hiệp thông sâu xa với Giáo hội Lữ Hành nơi trần thế và Giáo hội Đau Khổ nơi Luyện Ngục. Sách Khải Huyền mô tả cộng đoàn thiên quốc này là 'một đoàn người thật đông đảo không ai đếm xuể, thuộc mọi dân, mọi chi tộc, mọi nước và mọi ngôn ngữ, đang đứng trước ngai' (Kh 7,9).

Ngày lễ nhắc nhở mỗi Kitô hữu rằng sự thánh thiện có thể đạt được trong mọi bậc sống nhờ ân sủng của Đức Kitô. Trong Các Mối Phúc Thật được công bố trong bài Tin Mừng hôm nay, Chúa Giêsu đã trao cho chúng ta bản hiến chương thần linh để nên thánh.

liturgical.title_vi: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed (All Souls’ Day)

primary.title_en: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed (All Souls’ Day)
primary.title_vi: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed (All Souls’ Day)
primary.summary_en: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed, widely known as All Souls' Day, is a liturgical observance held on November 2 in the Latin Rite of the Catholic Church. This day is dedicated to praying for the faithful departed, particularly those believed to be in Purgatory. While not a Holy Day of Obligation, it carries a rank of Commemoration and is observed with the liturgical color violet.
primary.summary_vi: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed, widely known as All Souls' Day, is a liturgical observance held on November 2 in the Latin Rite of the Catholic Church. This day is dedicated to praying for the faithful departed, particularly those believed to be in Purgatory. While not a Holy Day of Obligation, it carries a rank of Commemoration and is observed with the liturgical color violet.
primary.body_en: On this day, the Church directs her attention toward the dead who have gone before us in faith. The liturgical focus shifts from the triumph of the saints (All Saints' Day, November 1) to the purification and rest of souls undergoing temporal punishment. Although the official readings for this specific commemoration are not printed in the daily USCCB calendar, the liturgy often utilizes texts concerning the resurrection and the hope of eternal life. Priests are traditionally permitted to celebrate three Masses, a privilege extended from the time of Pope Benedict XIV, allowing for the suffrage of many intentions for the dead.

liturgical.title_en: Tuesday of the 31th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Ba tuần 31 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Tuesday of the 31th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Ba tuần 31 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Tuesday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Tuesday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Tuesday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Tuesday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

liturgical.title_en: Saint Charles Borromeo, Bishop
liturgical.title_vi: Saint Charles Borromeo, Bishop

primary.title_en: Saint Charles Borromeo, Bishop
primary.title_vi: Saint Charles Borromeo, Bishop
primary.summary_en: Saint Charles Borromeo was a prominent bishop and cardinal of the sixteenth century who played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation. As the Archbishop of Milan, he implemented the reforms of the Council of Trent and is revered for his dedication to pastoral care and the education of the clergy.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Charles Borromeo was a prominent bishop and cardinal of the sixteenth century who played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation. As the Archbishop of Milan, he implemented the reforms of the Council of Trent and is revered for his dedication to pastoral care and the education of the clergy.
primary.body_en:
Charles Borromeo, born into a noble Italian family, chose the ecclesiastical state over secular power and was appointed Archbishop of Milan at a young age. He faced a diocese that had neglected its duties for decades and undertook the monumental task of revitalizing the spiritual and administrative life of the Church. His efforts included establishing seminaries, holding synods, and ensuring that the liturgical texts and catechisms were properly formed and accessible. The Church celebrates his feast to highlight the importance of episcopal vigilance and doctrinal clarity.

The readings appointed for this memorial, Philippians 2:12-18 and Luke 14:25-33, reflect the rigorous demands of Christian discipleship and the humility Christ exhibited. In the first reading, Paul urges believers to work out their salvation with fear and trembling, emphasizing that God works in them to will and act. In the Gospel, Jesus teaches about the cost of discipleship, urging potential followers to count the cost before building a tower or going to battle. These passages resonate with Borromeo's life of intense labor and unwavering commitment to the Church's mission, serving as a testament to his holiness.

primary.summary_en: The Thirty-second Sunday in Ordinary Time is the thirty-second Sunday of the liturgical year in the Roman Rite of the Catholic Church. It falls on November 8, 2026, within the twenty-second week of the liturgical year for the current cycle. The liturgical color is green, signifying growth and the passage of time. There are no optional memorials printed for this day in the USCCB calendar.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Chủ Nhật này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en: The Thirty-second Sunday in Ordinary Time emphasizes the Christian vocation to hope and perseverance. The readings for this Sunday in Year C focus on the resurrection of the dead and the eternal nature of God's covenant. The first reading from 2 Maccabees speaks of the brothers who died for their faith, confident in the Lord's justice. The Gospel, taken from Luke 20, presents the Sadducees' challenge to Jesus regarding marriage in the resurrection, where Jesus clarifies that the resurrected are like angels and children of God, living forever. The liturgy invites the faithful to contemplate the permanence of divine truth amidst temporal changes.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Sunday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

primary.summary_en: Celebrated on November 9, this feast honors the Cathedral of Rome, the mother and head of all churches. It marks the anniversary of the basilica's consecration and serves as a sign of unity with the See of Peter.
primary.summary_vi: Celebrated on November 9, this feast honors the Cathedral of Rome, the mother and head of all churches. It marks the anniversary of the basilica's consecration and serves as a sign of unity with the See of Peter.
primary.body_en: The Feast of the Dedication of the Lateran Basilica focuses on the Cathedral of Rome, officially known as the Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran. Although not the primary residence of the Pope, it is the cathedral church of the Bishop of Rome and holds a preeminent place among the minor basilicas of the Catholic Church. The liturgy invites the faithful to remember their baptismal promises and the spiritual temple they form together. Traditionally, the Gospel reading speaks of Jesus cleansing the Temple, emphasizing that the true house of God is built from living stones—believers themselves. Since this feast is not a Holy Day of Obligation, the daily readings for the current liturgical week apply unless a specific Proper is chosen, though the feast title remains fixed in the calendar.

primary.title_vi: Saint Leo the Great, Pope and Doctor of the Church
primary.summary_en: Saint Leo I, known as Leo the Great, served as Pope from 440 to 461 and is recognized for his profound theological writings and diplomatic skill. He famously met Attila the Hun to spare Rome from destruction and articulated the doctrine of the two natures of Christ at the Council of Chalcedon. Declared a Doctor of the Church, his sermons remain central to Catholic liturgy and theology.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Leo I, known as Leo the Great, served as Pope from 440 to 461 and is recognized for his profound theological writings and diplomatic skill. He famously met Attila the Hun to spare Rome from destruction and articulated the doctrine of the two natures of Christ at the Council of Chalcedon. Declared a Doctor of the Church, his sermons remain central to Catholic liturgy and theology.
primary.body_en: Pope Saint Leo the Great is celebrated for his pivotal role in defining the mystery of the Incarnation and for his steadfast defense of the Church's unity. His Tome to Flavian, which clarified the union of divine and human natures in the one Person of Jesus Christ, was affirmed by the Council of Chalcedon in 451. Beyond theology, Leo was a man of action who successfully negotiated with Attila the Hun, sparing Rome from sack and demonstrating the moral authority of the Papacy. His 96 surviving sermons and 143 letters exhibit a mastery of rhetoric that has influenced Christian thought for millennia. Today's readings from Titus and Luke call believers to humility and faithful service, echoing Leo's teaching that true leadership is rooted in service to God and neighbor.

primary.title_vi: Saint Martin of Tours, Bishop
primary.summary_en: Saint Martin of Tours, a former soldier who became a renowned bishop, is celebrated for his humility, monastic foundations, and defense of orthodoxy. His feast day commemorates his transition from military life to Christian service, symbolizing the call to peace and charity.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Martin of Tours, a former soldier who became a renowned bishop, is celebrated for his humility, monastic foundations, and defense of orthodoxy. His feast day commemorates his transition from military life to Christian service, symbolizing the call to peace and charity.
primary.body_en: Martin of Tours (c. 316–397) is one of the most venerated saints of the early Church, known for the act of dividing his cloak with a beggar, an event that prefigured his vision of Christ wearing that same half-cloak. After leaving the Roman army due to his Christian faith, he became a disciple of Saint Hilary of Poitiers and founded one of the first monasteries in Gaul at Ligugé. As Bishop of Tours, he was a tireless evangelizer who combated Arianism and cared deeply for the poor. The liturgical readings for this day, specifically Luke 17:11-19, highlight the theme of gratitude and faith, reflecting Martin’s lifelong journey from a soldier’s rigid discipline to a bishop’s compassionate faith. His life remains a testament to the possibility of integrating martial discipline with monastic simplicity and episcopal responsibility.

primary.title_en: Saint Josaphat, Bishop and Martyr
primary.title_vi: Saint Josaphat, Bishop and Martyr
primary.summary_en: Saint Josaphat Kuncevych was a Ruthenian bishop who dedicated his life to the reconciliation of the Eastern and Western churches and was martyred in 1623. His feast is celebrated as a Memorial in the Roman Catholic liturgical calendar. The liturgical readings for this day include Phlm 7-20 and Lk 17:20-25.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Josaphat Kuncevych was a Ruthenian bishop who dedicated his life to the reconciliation of the Eastern and Western churches and was martyred in 1623. His feast is celebrated as a Memorial in the Roman Catholic liturgical calendar. The liturgical readings for this day include Phlm 7-20 and Lk 17:20-25.
primary.body_en: Josaphat Kuncevych was born in Volodymyr-Volynskyi and became a Basilian monk, later serving as the archbishop of Polotsk. He worked tirelessly to unify the Ruthenian people with Rome while maintaining their Byzantine liturgical traditions, a stance that led to violent opposition from those who rejected union. He was murdered by attackers with axes in Vitebsk on November 14, 1623, and was canonized by Pope Pius VII in 1867. Today, he is honored as a model of ecumenical dialogue and sacrifice, with his relics resting in St. Peter's Basilica. The liturgical texts for this Memorial, specifically Phlm 7-20 and Lk 17:20-25, reflect themes of fraternal love and the hidden nature of the Kingdom of God, resonating with Josaphat's life of quiet fidelity amidst conflict.

primary.title_en: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, Virgin
primary.title_vi: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, Virgin
primary.summary_en: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, the first United States citizen to be canonized by the Catholic Church, is remembered for her tireless missionary work among Italian immigrants in North and South America. Her legacy is defined by the founding of the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart and her establishment of numerous schools, hospitals, and orphanages that served the poor and displaced. She is recognized as the patron saint of immigrants, embodying a profound commitment to social justice and spiritual care for those far from home.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, the first United States citizen to be canonized by the Catholic Church, is remembered for her tireless missionary work among Italian immigrants in North and South America. Her legacy is defined by the founding of the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart and her establishment of numerous schools, hospitals, and orphanages that served the poor and displaced. She is recognized as the patron saint of immigrants, embodying a profound commitment to social justice and spiritual care for those far from home.
primary.body_en:
The Memorial of Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini highlights a pivotal figure in the history of American Catholicism and the diaspora of Italian migrants. Born in Lombardy, Italy, she answered a call to mission that led her across the Atlantic, where she dedicated her life to uplifting immigrants through education, healthcare, and spiritual formation. Her work extended beyond mere charity; she institutionalized care by founding houses in cities such as New York, Buenos Aires, and Paris, ensuring that the sacred heart of Jesus remained central to the lives of the marginalized.

In the liturgy for this day, the Church invites the faithful to reflect on Cabrini's virtue of hope and her unwavering trust in Divine Providence amidst logistical and cultural hardships. While the USCCB 2026 calendar marks her as a Memorial on this Friday, November 13, 2026, it does not print specific proper readings, signaling that the community may use the weekday readings of the Thirty-second Week in Ordinary Time. Her intercession is sought not only for immigrants but for all who navigate the challenges of cultural displacement and seek to build communities grounded in faith and solidarity.

liturgical.title_en: Monday of the 32th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Hai tuần 32 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Monday of the 32th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Hai tuần 32 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Monday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Monday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Monday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Monday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

liturgical.title_en: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, Religious
liturgical.title_vi: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, Religious

primary.title_en: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, Religious
primary.title_vi: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, Religious
primary.summary_en: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary was a devout member of the Third Order of Saint Francis and a daughter of King Andrew II. She is renowned for her profound humility, extreme asceticism, and dedication to the poor after the death of her husband. Her life exemplifies the integration of royal dignity with Franciscan simplicity. She is commemorated on this Tuesday in the Ordinary Time calendar.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary was a devout member of the Third Order of Saint Francis and a daughter of King Andrew II. She is renowned for her profound humility, extreme asceticism, and dedication to the poor after the death of her husband. Her life exemplifies the integration of royal dignity with Franciscan simplicity. She is commemorated on this Tuesday in the Ordinary Time calendar.
primary.body_en:
Born in 1207 and passing away in 1231, Elizabeth of Hungary is venerated for her transformative journey from a princess to a widow serving the destitute. She married Louis IV, Landgrave of Thuringia, and bore him three children, but after his death, she renounced her status and devoted herself to caring for the sick and hungry. Known as 'Saint Elizabeth of the Hungarians,' she founded hospitals and shelters, embodying the Christian virtue of caritas.

The liturgical readings for this day, Revelation 3:1-6, 14-22 and Luke 19:1-10, resonate with her life's narrative. The Gospel account of Zacchaeus, a tax collector who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, mirrors Elizabeth's humility in lowering herself from royal heights to serve Christ in the poor. The call to repentance and generous restitution in the Gospel parallels her radical redistribution of wealth and her unwavering commitment to spiritual poverty despite her worldly title.

liturgical.title_en: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
liturgical.title_vi: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

primary.title_en: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
primary.title_vi: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
primary.summary_en: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a memorial celebrated on November 21. It commemorates the dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major and the presentation of the young Mary in the Temple. The liturgy uses the white color and specific readings to highlight her role in salvation history.
primary.summary_vi: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a memorial celebrated on November 21. It commemorates the dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major and the presentation of the young Mary in the Temple. The liturgy uses the white color and specific readings to highlight her role in salvation history.
primary.body_en: This memorial focuses on the early life of the Blessed Virgin Mary, specifically her presentation in the Temple at a young age, an event rooted in tradition rather than explicit Scripture. Although not recorded in the canonical Gospels, the story comes from the apocryphal Protoevangelium of James. The Church uses this day to reflect on the total dedication of Mary to God, which prepared her to become the Mother of Jesus. The liturgical color is white, signifying joy and purity. The readings for the day often include Revelation 11:4-12 and Luke 20:27-40, connecting the sanctity of the Temple with the resurrection of the dead.

liturgical.title_en: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
liturgical.title_vi: Chúa Giêsu Kitô Vua Vũ Trụ

primary.title_en: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
primary.title_vi: Chúa Giêsu Kitô Vua Vũ Trụ
primary.summary_en: On the final Sunday of the liturgical year, Catholics celebrate Jesus Christ as King of the Universe. Matthew 25 connects his kingship with mercy shown to the hungry, the stranger, the sick, and the imprisoned.
primary.summary_vi: Vào Chúa nhật cuối năm phụng vụ, người Công giáo mừng kính Chúa Giêsu Kitô là Vua Vũ Trụ. Tin Mừng Matthêu chương 25 nối kết vương quyền của Người với lòng thương xót dành cho người đói khát, khách lạ, người đau yếu và người bị giam cầm.
primary.body_en:
The prophet Ezekiel presents God as a shepherd who seeks the lost and tends those in need. In the First Letter to the Corinthians, Paul proclaims the risen Christ and the final defeat of death.

In Matthew 25, Jesus describes the judgment of the nations through the image of a shepherd separating sheep and goats. His followers are called to recognize him in people who need food, welcome, care, and compassion.

The solemnity of Christ the King closes the liturgical year with a practical invitation: let justice, mercy, and love shape everyday life.
primary.body_vi:
Ngôn sứ Êdêkien nói về Thiên Chúa như vị mục tử tìm kiếm những con chiên lạc và chăm sóc người yếu đau. Trong thư gửi tín hữu Côrintô, thánh Phaolô công bố Đức Kitô phục sinh và chiến thắng sau cùng trước sự chết.

Tin Mừng theo thánh Matthêu chương 25 diễn tả cuộc phán xét bằng hình ảnh người mục tử phân biệt các chiên. Người môn đệ được mời gọi nhận ra Đức Kitô nơi những người cần được giúp đỡ.

Lễ Chúa Kitô Vua Vũ Trụ kết thúc năm phụng vụ bằng một lời mời gọi cụ thể: sống đức công chính, lòng thương xót và tình yêu thương trong đời thường.

liturgical.title_en: Monday of the 33th Week in Ordinary Time
liturgical.title_vi: Thứ Hai tuần 33 Mùa Thường Niên

primary.title_en: Monday of the 33th Week in Ordinary Time
primary.title_vi: Thứ Hai tuần 33 Mùa Thường Niên
primary.summary_en: This Monday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Ordinary Time. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Monday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Thường Niên. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Ordinary Time, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Monday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Thường Niên, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Monday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

liturgical.title_en: Memorial of Saint Andrew Dũng-Lạc, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs
liturgical.title_vi: Lễ Kính Các Thánh Tử Đạo Việt Nam — Thánh Anrê Dũng-Lạc, Linh mục và các Bạn Tử đạo

primary.title_en: Memorial of Saint Andrew Dũng-Lạc, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs
primary.title_vi: Lễ Kính Các Thánh Tử Đạo Việt Nam — Thánh Anrê Dũng-Lạc, Linh mục và các Bạn Tử đạo
primary.summary_en: Saint Andrew Dũng-Lạc (1795–1839) and his 116 companion martyrs bore heroic witness to Jesus Christ during brutal persecutions in Vietnam under the Nguyễn dynasty. Canonized by Pope John Paul II in 1988, these martyrs represent bishops, priests, religious, and lay faithful who chose torture and martyrdom rather than trample upon the Cross.
primary.summary_vi: Thánh Anrê Dũng-Lạc (1795–1839) và 116 Bạn Tử Đạo đã làm chứng anh dũng cho Chúa Giêsu Kitô trong những cuộc bách hại khốc liệt tại Việt Nam dưới triều Nguyễn. Được Đức Giáo hoàng Gioan Phaolô II tôn phong hiển thánh năm 1988, các ngài gồm các giám mục, linh mục, tu sĩ và giáo dân đã can đảm chịu trăm chiều tra tấn và cái chết chứ quyết không đạp lên Thánh Giá.
primary.body_en:
Christianity was first brought to Vietnam in the sixteenth century by Portuguese, Spanish Dominican, and French MEP missionaries. Despite fierce persecution under Emperors Minh Mạng, Thiệu Trị, and Tự Đức between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries, over 100,000 Vietnamese Christians sealed their faith with their blood.

Andrew Dũng-Lạc was born into a poor non-Christian family and was educated by a Catholic catechist. Ordained a priest in 1823, he served faithfully as a parish priest, repeatedly captured and ransomed by parishioners so he could continue administering the Sacraments in secret. In 1839, he was arrested alongside Father Peter Thi and beheaded in Hanoi on December 21.

On June 19, 1988, Pope Saint John Paul II canonized 117 Vietnamese martyrs in Rome. Their heroic fidelity remains the glorious foundation and spiritual inspiration of the Catholic Church in Vietnam and the global Vietnamese diaspora.
primary.body_vi:
Đức tin Kitô giáo được truyền bá vào Việt Nam từ thế kỷ XVI qua các thừa sai Dòng Đa Minh, Dòng Tên và Hội Thừa Sai Paris (MEP). Bất chấp những cuộc bách hại khốc liệt dưới triều các vua Minh Mạng, Thiệu Trị và Tự Đức giữa thế kỷ XVII và XIX, hơn 100.000 Kitô hữu Việt Nam đã can đảm lấy máu mình để minh chứng cho niềm tin son sắt.

Thánh Anrê Dũng-Lạc sinh ra trong một gia đình nghèo ngoại giáo và được một thầy giảng Công giáo nhận nuôi dưỡng, dạy dỗ. Thụ phong linh mục năm 1823, ngài tận tụy chăn dắt các giáo xứ, nhiều lần bị bắt rồi được giáo dân chuộc về để ngài tiếp tục âm thầm ban các Bí tích. Năm 1839, ngài bị bắt cùng Linh mục Phêrô Trương Văn Thi và bị trảm quyết tại Cầu Giấy (Hà Nội) vào ngày 21 tháng 12.

Ngày 19 tháng 6 năm 1988, Đức Giáo hoàng Gioan Phaolô II đã long trọng tôn phong 117 Thánh Tử Đạo Việt Nam lên bậc Hiển Thánh tại Rôma. Sự trung kiên anh dũng của các ngài là nền tảng vinh quang và là nguồn linh hứng thiêng liêng cho Giáo hội Công giáo Việt Nam và cộng đồng Công giáo Việt Nam trên toàn thế giới.

app_hooks.hero_line_vi: Hạt giống đức tin trổ sinh từ dòng máu hào hùng của Các Thánh Tử Đạo Việt Nam
app_hooks.prayer_prompt_en: O God, source and origin of all fatherhood, who kept the Holy Martyrs Andrew Dũng-Lạc and his companions faithful to the Cross of Your Son even to the shedding of their blood, grant through their intercession that we may spread Your love among all peoples.
app_hooks.prayer_prompt_vi: Lạy Thiên Chúa là nguồn gốc mọi quyền phụ tử, Đấng đã gìn giữ Các Thánh Tử Đạo Anrê Dũng-Lạc và các bạn luôn trung kiên với Thánh Giá Con Một Chúa cho đến giọt máu cuối cùng, xin vì lời chuyển cầu của các ngài cho chúng con biết loan truyền tình yêu Chúa giữa muôn dân.

liturgical.title_en: Saint Andrew, Apostle
liturgical.title_vi: Saint Andrew, Apostle

primary.title_en: Saint Andrew, Apostle
primary.title_vi: Saint Andrew, Apostle
primary.summary_en: On November 30, the Catholic Church celebrates the Feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle, the first called of the disciples and brother of Saint Peter. As a Feast, this day holds significant liturgical weight, marked by the color red to signify apostolic martyrdom and the proclamation of the Gospel.
primary.summary_vi: On November 30, the Catholic Church celebrates the Feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle, the first called of the disciples and brother of Saint Peter. As a Feast, this day holds significant liturgical weight, marked by the color red to signify apostolic martyrdom and the proclamation of the Gospel.
primary.body_en: Saint Andrew, whose name means 'manly' or 'brave,' is revered as the Protokletos, or 'First-called,' for being the first disciple to follow Jesus. The liturgy for this day traditionally emphasizes his role in bringing Peter to Christ and his steadfast evangelism. The readings from Romans 10:9-18 and Matthew 4:18-22 highlight the universal call to proclaim the Lord and the immediate response of the fishermen brothers to Jesus' invitation.

primary.summary_en: Saint Francis Xavier, a co-founder of the Society of Jesus, is celebrated for his extensive missionary work in Asia. He is regarded as one of the greatest missionaries in Christian history.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Francis Xavier, a co-founder of the Society of Jesus, is celebrated for his extensive missionary work in Asia. He is regarded as one of the greatest missionaries in Christian history.
primary.body_en: Saint Francis Xavier, born in the Kingdom of Navarre, dedicated his life to spreading the Gospel in India and Japan. As a companion of Saint Ignatius of Loyola, he helped establish the Jesuit Order. His liturgical memorial emphasizes the urgency of evangelization and the importance of foundational Christian teaching, mirrored in the day's readings from Isaiah and Matthew regarding obedience to God's word.

liturgical.title_en: Saint Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor of the Church
liturgical.title_vi: Saint Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

primary.title_en: Saint Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor of the Church
primary.title_vi: Saint Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor of the Church
primary.summary_en: Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan and a Doctor of the Church, is commemorated on this memorial day. Known for his rhetorical skill and influence on Saint Augustine, he established foundational liturgical practices in the Western Church.
primary.summary_vi: Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan and a Doctor of the Church, is commemorated on this memorial day. Known for his rhetorical skill and influence on Saint Augustine, he established foundational liturgical practices in the Western Church.
primary.body_en: Ambrose, a former Roman governor who became Bishop of Milan against his own inclination, played a pivotal role in shaping the early Church's identity and liturgy. He is credited with composing hymns that remain in use and for his defense of orthodoxy against Arianism. The liturgical readings for this day, Is 35:1-10 and Lk 5:17-26, highlight the theme of divine healing and the restoration of God's people, resonating with Ambrose's own journey from secular administration to spiritual leadership.
primary.body_vi: Ambrose, a former Roman governor who became Bishop of Milan against his own inclination, played a pivotal role in shaping the early Church's identity and liturgy. He is credited with composing hymns that remain in use and for his defense of orthodoxy against Arianism. The liturgical readings for this day, Is 35:1-10 and Lk 5:17-26, highlight the theme of divine healing and the restoration of God's people, resonating with Ambrose's own journey from secular administration to spiritual leadership.

liturgical.title_en: Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary
liturgical.title_vi: Đại Lễ Đức Mẹ Vô Nhiễm Nguyên Tội

primary.title_en: Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary
primary.title_vi: Đại Lễ Đức Mẹ Vô Nhiễm Nguyên Tội
primary.summary_en: On December 8, Catholics celebrate the Immaculate Conception: Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her own conception through the grace of God and the merits of Jesus Christ. Pope Pius IX defined this dogma in 1854, and the feast is celebrated during Advent.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày 8 tháng 12, người Công giáo mừng kính Đức Mẹ Vô Nhiễm Nguyên Tội: nhờ ân sủng Thiên Chúa và công nghiệp Chúa Giêsu Kitô, Đức Maria được gìn giữ khỏi tội nguyên tổ ngay từ giây phút đầu tiên được thụ thai. Đức Giáo hoàng Piô IX định tín giáo lý này năm 1854, và ngày lễ được cử hành trong Mùa Vọng.
primary.body_en:
In 1854, Pope Pius IX defined the dogma of the Immaculate Conception in Ineffabilis Deus. It concerns Mary's own conception, not the conception of Jesus, and teaches that her preservation from original sin was a gift of grace through Christ.

Catholic devotion also remembers the apparitions reported by Bernadette Soubirous at Lourdes in 1858. These accounts belong to the Church's devotional tradition and are not the historical basis for the earlier dogmatic definition.

Celebrated during Advent, the solemnity invites reflection on the initiative of God's grace and the hope of salvation.
primary.body_vi:
Năm 1854, Đức Giáo hoàng Piô IX định tín Đức Mẹ Vô Nhiễm Nguyên Tội trong văn kiện Ineffabilis Deus. Tín điều nói về việc chính Đức Maria được thụ thai, không phải việc Chúa Giêsu được thụ thai, và dạy rằng Mẹ được gìn giữ khỏi tội nguyên tổ nhờ ân sủng Thiên Chúa và công nghiệp Đức Kitô.

Trong truyền thống sùng kính Công giáo, tín hữu cũng tưởng nhớ những cuộc hiện ra được Bernadette Soubirous thuật lại tại Lộ Đức năm 1858. Những trình thuật này thuộc đời sống đạo đức và không phải là cơ sở lịch sử của việc định tín đã diễn ra trước đó.

Được cử hành trong Mùa Vọng, lễ trọng mời gọi suy niệm về ân sủng đi bước trước của Thiên Chúa và niềm hy vọng cứu độ.
primary.confidence_note_en: The USCCB identifies December 8, 2026 as the Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception. The Catechism (§491) attributes the 1854 definition to Pius IX; Lourdes accounts are marked as devotion/tradition.
primary.confidence_note_vi: USCCB xác nhận ngày 8 tháng 12 năm 2026 là lễ trọng Đức Mẹ Vô Nhiễm Nguyên Tội. Sách Giáo lý (§491) ghi nhận việc Đức Piô IX định tín năm 1854; các trình thuật Lộ Đức được nêu là truyền thống sùng kính.

primary.summary_en: On December 12, the Church celebrates the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, commemorating her apparitions to Saint Juan Diego in 1531 on Tepeyac Hill. This feast honors her as the patroness of the Americas and highlights her role in the evangelization of Mexico and the conversion of the indigenous people. The liturgical focus is on her intercession and the miracle of the roses and the image on the tilma.
primary.summary_vi: On December 12, the Church celebrates the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, commemorating her apparitions to Saint Juan Diego in 1531 on Tepeyac Hill. This feast honors her as the patroness of the Americas and highlights her role in the evangelization of Mexico and the conversion of the indigenous people. The liturgical focus is on her intercession and the miracle of the roses and the image on the tilma.
primary.body_en: The Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe is a major celebration in the Universal Church, particularly in the Americas, recognizing the profound spiritual and cultural impact of the Virgin Mary's apparition to the humble indigenous peasant, Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin. The liturgy invites the faithful to reflect on her title as the 'Mother of the True God Who Gives Life' and her request for a church to be built in her honor at Tepeyac. Central to the devotion is the miraculous image imprinted on Juan Diego's tilma, which serves as a visual catechesis, blending Christian theology with indigenous symbols to proclaim the Gospel. The day’s prayers often emphasize humility, evangelization, and the maternal care of Mary for all peoples, regardless of race or status, as she stands with hands folded in prayer, surrounded by the rays of the sun and crowned with twelve stars.

liturgical.title_en: 3th Sunday of Advent
liturgical.title_vi: Chúa Nhật tuần 3 Mùa Vọng

primary.title_en: 3th Sunday of Advent
primary.title_vi: Chúa Nhật tuần 3 Mùa Vọng
primary.summary_en: This Sunday falls within the sacred liturgical season of Advent. The Church offers the daily readings and prayers of the Roman Missal to guide the faithful in continuous communion with Jesus Christ. Through daily prayer and acts of charity, believers sanctify their daily work.
primary.summary_vi: Ngày Sunday này nằm trong mùa phụng vụ thánh thiện Mùa Vọng. Giáo hội trao ban các bài đọc và lời nguyện hàng ngày trong Sách Lễ Rôma để dẫn dắt các tín hữu trong sự hiệp thông liên lỉ với Chúa Giêsu Kitô. Qua lời cầu nguyện và đức bác ái, người tín hữu thánh hóa công việc mỗi ngày.
primary.body_en:
The Catholic liturgical year is structured to immerse the faithful into the full mystery of Jesus Christ, from His Incarnation and public ministry to His Passion, Death, and Resurrection. During Advent, the daily readings draw our hearts into reflection on the Gospel.

On this Sunday, the Mass readings invite believers to examine their conscience, seek reconciliation, and practice genuine compassion toward their family and community. The prayers of the liturgy lift up the needs of the whole human family before the throne of God.

Whether engaged in manual labor, intellectual study, or quiet contemplation, Christians are called to offer every action for the glory of God. In this way, ordinary moments are consecrated into living sacrifices pleasing to the Lord.
primary.body_vi:
Năm phụng vụ Công giáo được thiết lập để đưa các tín hữu đi sâu vào trọn vẹn mầu nhiệm Chúa Giêsu Kitô, từ lúc Nhập Thể, thi hành sứ vụ công khai đến Cuộc Khổ Nạn, Cái Chết và Phục Sinh vinh hiển. Trong Mùa Vọng, các bài đọc hàng ngày hướng tâm hồn chúng ta suy niệm sâu xa về Tin Mừng.

Vào ngày Sunday này, các bài đọc Thánh Lễ mời gọi người tín hữu xét mình, tìm kiếm ơn giao hòa và thực thi lòng thương xót chân thành đối với gia đình và xã hội. Lời nguyện phụng vụ dâng lên trước ngai tòa Thiên Chúa mọi nhu cầu của toàn thể gia đình nhân loại.

Dù đang lao động chân tay, học tập hay chiêm niệm thinh lặng, người Kitô hữu được kêu gọi dâng mọi việc làm để tôn vinh Thiên Chúa. Nhờ đó, những giây phút bình dị nhất được thánh hiến thành của lễ sống động đẹp lòng Chúa.

liturgical.title_en: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church
liturgical.title_vi: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church

primary.title_en: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church
primary.title_vi: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church
primary.summary_en: On December 14, the Church celebrates Saint John of the Cross, the great Carmelite reformer, mystic, and Doctor of the Church. His life was marked by deep union with God and profound poetry, leading to significant reforms within the Carmelite Order.
primary.summary_vi: On December 14, the Church celebrates Saint John of the Cross, the great Carmelite reformer, mystic, and Doctor of the Church. His life was marked by deep union with God and profound poetry, leading to significant reforms within the Carmelite Order.
primary.body_en: Saint John of the Cross (1542–1591), born Juan de Yepes y Álvarez, was a Spanish mystic and poet who, alongside Teresa of Ávila, reformed the Carmelite Order. He is celebrated for his profound writings, including 'The Ascent of Mount Carmel' and 'The Dark Night of the Soul,' which describe the soul’s journey to divine union. Proclaimed a Doctor of the Church in 1926, his teachings emphasize the importance of detachment and interior silence to achieve perfect charity. The liturgical readings for this day, Nm 24:2-7, 15-17a and Mt 21:23-27, invite reflection on God’s providence and the authority of Christ’s teaching, themes central to John’s mystical theology.
primary.body_vi: Saint John of the Cross (1542–1591), born Juan de Yepes y Álvarez, was a Spanish mystic and poet who, alongside Teresa of Ávila, reformed the Carmelite Order. Proclaimed a Doctor of the Church in 1926, his teachings emphasize the importance of detachment and interior silence to achieve perfect charity. The liturgical readings for this day, Nm 24:2-7, 15-17a and Mt 21:23-27, invite reflection on God’s providence and the authority of Christ’s teaching, themes central to John’s mystical theology.
